guidelinesCompliance.guideline: Use red-green-refactor TDD and reproduce the no-include adopter failure before implementation.
guidelinesCompliance.evidence: The initial no-include e2e failed at nested ai-preflight; the same test now completes failure/retry/archive.

guidelinesCompliance.guideline: Propagate one validated argv boundary; do not encode shell command strings or trust ambient MAKEFLAGS to preserve -f.
guidelinesCompliance.evidence: scripts/ai_common.py nested_make_command constructs list argv and Makefiles export firstword MAKEFILE_LIST.

guidelinesCompliance.guideline: Keep canonical registered check/evidence commands repository-relative and machine-independent.
guidelinesCompliance.evidence: ai_finish records catalog command identity while only subprocess argv receives the repository-relative -f selection.

guidelinesCompliance.guideline: Fail closed on conflicting or untrusted entrypoint authority rather than silently falling back to plain make.
guidelinesCompliance.evidence: The table-driven negative matrix rejects external, traversal, missing, unsupported, and conflicting forms.

guidelinesCompliance.guideline: Keep the root Makefile and distributed templates/make/Makefile.ai behavior aligned.
guidelinesCompliance.evidence: tests/test_makefile.py verifies identical export/recursive invariants and absence of legacy call forms.

risk.detail: The Make entrypoint is execution authority; validation, no-fallback behavior, and included-root compatibility are regression-guarded.

observedIssues.fact: The red adopter journey proved ai_start.py reached ai-preflight with plain make and failed because the root Makefile did not include AI Cockpit.
observedIssues.decision: Propagate one repository-local selected Makefile through Python callers rather than requiring a root edit.
observedIssues.resolution: Shared argv construction makes the same explicit entrypoint available to start, finish, onboarding, and hosted verification.
observedIssues.followUp: Require Hosted CI and full lifecycle closure.

observedIssues.fact: After the Python boundary was fixed, the same red journey reached ai-preflight but Make recipes still launched /usr/bin/make without -f.
observedIssues.decision: Replace all recursive command sites with AI_NESTED_MAKE bound to the exported selected entrypoint.
observedIssues.resolution: Static parity tests reject both legacy command-v lookup and ambient MAKE fallback forms.
observedIssues.followUp: Full quality exercises every recursive quality and lifecycle path.

observedIssues.fact: The platform Make executable path contains spaces; the first recursive implementation invoked it unquoted and failed before target lookup.
observedIssues.decision: Quote the Make executable and selected entrypoint independently in Make recipes while retaining list argv in Python.
observedIssues.resolution: The no-include journey passes on the current Xcode toolchain path and static Make tests retain the quoting invariant.
observedIssues.followUp: Hosted macOS and compatibility checks provide external confirmation.

observedIssues.fact: The first ai-finish stopped before full quality because scripts/ai_start.py was covered by the adopter e2e but its configured production-to-test association required tests/test_start_and_archive.py.
observedIssues.decision: Keep the association strict and add a direct ai_start.run_make regression instead of weakening the Coverage Guard.
observedIssues.resolution: The selected explicit entrypoint is now proven both by the full adopter journey and the canonical start/archive test surface.
observedIssues.followUp: Restart ai-finish from the beginning with a fresh Contract-bound checkpoint.

observedIssues.fact: The first complete quality run passed 1391 tests but Bandit reported the same count with a changed digest: the literal Make option -f was misclassified as B105 while the validated argv variable no longer emitted the prior scanner-only B607 identity.
observedIssues.decision: Suppress only the proven -f false positive, review the old and new normalized finding sets, and update the low-risk baseline to the resulting smaller set rather than regenerating it blindly.
observedIssues.resolution: The Make option carries a narrow B105 nosec rationale; the baseline records the reviewed 111-finding set and the dedicated gate must pass before full ai-finish is restarted.
observedIssues.followUp: Run the focused Bandit baseline gate, refresh Contract-bound checkpoints, then restart complete ai-finish.

residualRisks.detail: Behavior is verified with the repository's supported GNU Make environments; unusual non-GNU Make implementations remain governed by compatibility CI.
